mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in one month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increases > 0.5pp do not correlate with subsequent economic weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals a recessionary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or GDPC1 declines do not correlate with subsequent recessionary periods.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month signals supply chain disruptions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO drops > 2% MoM do not correlate with subsequent supply chain issues.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is rising, it signals a potential overheating economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of low FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL does not correlate with subsequent negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) for three consecutive months signals economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increases do not correlate with subsequent economic strength.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% month-over-month signals increased consumer confidence and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increases > 10% MoM do not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is rising and real GDP (GDPC1) is declining, it signals a tightening monetary policy in a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: tightening monetary policy in a weakening economy
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of rising FEDFUNDS and declining GDPC1 does not correlate with subsequent negative returns.
